title: CRLR/690/2022 of BABLI BALMIKI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME, DEHRADUN

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.690 of 2022
Babli Balmiki alias Umesh Saran ..........Revisionist
Vs.
State Uttarakhand and another ........ Respondents

Present : Mr. P.C. Petshali and Mr. Yogesh Upadhyay, Advocates for the
revisionist.
 Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. with Mr. Dinesh Chauhan and Ms.
Shivali Joshi, Brief Holders for the State.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
Judgment and Order dated 19.05.2018, passed in Misc.
Criminal Case No.397 of 2017, Smt. Neetu vs. Babli
Balmiki alias Umesh Saran, by the court of Judge, Family
Court, District Nainital (for short, "the case") as well as
the Order dated 24.09.2022, passed in Misc. Criminal
Case No.237 of 2022, Smt. Neetu vs. Babli Balmiki,
passed by the Court of Family Court, Haridwar (for short,
"the misc. case").
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.

2
3. The record reveals that initially the private
respondent filed an application under Section 125 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, "the Code")
seeking maintenance, based on which, the proceeding of
Case No.49 of 2000 was instituted, which was decided on
05.02.2001 and the revisionist was directed to pay `300/-
per month as maintenance to the private respondent.
Subsequent to it, the private respondent filed an
application under Section 127 of the Code seeking
enhancement of the maintenance granted to her, based
on which, the proceeding of Case No.130 of 2004 was
instituted and vide order dated 24.06.2005, the amount
of the interim maintenance was enhanced from `300/- to
`600/- per month. The private respondent again moved
an application seeking enhancement of interim
maintenance, which is basis of the case.
4. It has been the case of the private respondent
that the revisionist has been working as a Sweeper in an
Insurance Company at Rampur and gets `33,500/- per
month salary whereas, the private respondent is not able
to maintain herself with the aid of the maintenance
amount, which she is getting.

3
5. The revisionist was given notice of the case.
The revisionist did not appear. The case proceeded ex
parte. The private respondent filed an affidavit in support
of her averments. After hearing the private respondent
and the material placed before the court, the amount of
maintenance has been increased from `600/- to
`10,000/- per month. It appears that the revisionist did
not pay the maintenance. That is how the private
respondent filed an application seeking recovery of the
arrears, which is basis of the misc. case. In the misc.
case, notices were issued to the revisionist. He initially
appeared. But, on 24.09.2022, he remained absent and
recovery warrants have already been issued against him.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the amount of maintenance which has been
enhanced, is too high. The revisionist is not in a position
to pay that amount. He has other responsibilities and
liabilities also.
7. It is argued that out of `17,000/- which is the
income of the revisionist, he has been directed to pay
`10,000/- per month to the private respondent, which is
not proportionally divided. It is also submitted that in the

4
misc. case the revisionist had filed objections, but it was
not considered.
8. In her application under Section 127 of the
Code, the private respondent has led evidence. She had
produced information with regard to the salary of the
revisionist under the Right to Information Act, 2005. In
para 9 of the Judgment and order dated 19.05.2018, the
Court has observed that, in fact, the salary of the
revisionist in the year 2018 was `30,022.02/- per month
out of which there was some deduction and he was
getting `17,319/- per month.
9. The court has taken note of the deduction and
has noted that amount of deduction would be available to
the revisionist himself. In fact, the revisionist did not opt
to appear in the case. The evidence was un-rebutted. Out
of `30,000/- more than 30% deduction is for what? it is
not explained. Is it compulsory deduction? Therefore, this
court cannot speculate about the deductions. Cannot the
revisionist reduce the deduction which was made from his
salary? The fact remains that the salary of the revisionist
in the year 2018 was about `30,000/- per month. The
amount of maintenance under Section 125 of the Code

5
was awarded to the private respondent in the year 2005
that was `600/-.
10. Keeping in view the entirety of facts, the court
below has rightly enhanced the amount from `600/- to
`10,000/- per month.
11. Therefore, there is no reason to make any
interference in the order dated 19.05.2018 passed in the
case.
12. The recovery proceedings were initiated in the
year 2022. The revisionist did appear in the proceeding,
but again he remained absent. It was the revisionist to
show that why recovery should not be made from him?
Therefore the court had no option except to issue a
recovery warrants against him. There also appears to be
no reason to make interference in the order dated
24.09.2022, passed in the misc. case.
13. In fact, it is much pathetic that despite an
order of maintenance against the revisionist, the
revisionist has been able to delay the recovery of it. The
order of enhancement was passed in the case on
19.05.2018. It is being challenged after 05 years while
taking shelter to order dated 24.09.2022, passed in the

6
misc. case. The Court expects that the recovery is
expedited and all the arrears are paid to the private
respondent within a shortest possible time.
14. With the above observation, the revision is
dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 18.04.2023
Sanjay
